Shopify setup guide

Move Freely

How to load your 13 summer emails into Shopify, check them and schedule them.

For Jess and Dan · X-ZONE New Zealand
Sends from 26 November 2026 to 18 February 2027

Before you start

Setting up the first email takes about 30 minutes. After that, each one takes about 10. Do it on a computer, not a phone: Shopify's code editor only works on a desktop.

What you have

  • 13 email files, one per week: xzone-email-w01.html to xzone-email-w13.html
  • An images folder with 16 pictures: the logo, 13 hero photos, your photo and the range photo
  • The approval page, showing every email as it will look

What you need

  • Shopify admin access with Shopify Email (now called Shopify Messaging) installed
  • A plain text editor: TextEdit on a Mac or Notepad on Windows
  • Your business address, which the law requires in every marketing email
  • The dates and offers listed on the approval page under "Please confirm"
How it works. Each email is a finished design written in code. You upload the pictures to Shopify once, tell each email where they are, fill in a few gaps such as dates, then import the file into Shopify. Shopify sends it to your subscribers.

Part 1: Do this once

1

Upload the pictures to Shopify

  1. In Shopify admin, go to Content → Files.
  2. Click Upload files and select every picture in the images folder.
  3. Keep the file names exactly as they are. The emails look for these names.

2

Find your Files folder address

Each email needs to know where your pictures live on Shopify. You find that address once and reuse it in every email.

  1. In Content → Files, find xzone-email-logo.png and click its copy link icon.
  2. Paste the link somewhere you can edit it, for example a note. It will look like this:
https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0123/4567/8901/files/xzone-email-logo.png?v=1732512345
  1. Delete the file name and everything after it (the grey part). Keep the slash at the end:
https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0123/4567/8901/files/

This is your Files folder address. Save it in your note. The numbers above are an example; yours will be different.

Part 2: For each email

Repeat these steps for each of the 13 emails, using the schedule on the last page. Start with No. 01.

3

Open the email file and add the folder address

  1. Right-click the email file (for example xzone-email-w01.html) and choose Open With → TextEdit (Mac) or Notepad (Windows). Don't double-click it, because that opens it in a browser.
  2. Near the top, find this line:
{% assign img = "PASTE-SHOPIFY-FILES-FOLDER-URL-HERE/" %}
  1. Replace the highlighted text with your Files folder address. Keep the quote marks. It should end up like this:
{% assign img = "https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0123/4567/8901/files/" %}
Mac users: if TextEdit shows the email as a picture instead of code, go to TextEdit → Settings → Open and Save and tick Display HTML files as HTML code instead of formatted text. Then open the file again.
4

Fill in the gaps

Use Find (Cmd+F on a Mac, Ctrl+F on Windows) to search for [ and replace every word in square brackets:

  • [business address] in the footer of every email
  • Dates and offers such as [date] or [offer] in some emails (listed on the last page)

Button links. Every button currently goes to https://www.xzone.nz/. Search for that address and replace it with the page you want, for example a product page. Adding tracking tags shows you which sales came from the email:

https://www.xzone.nz/products/x-zone-joints-rub?utm_source=shopify&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=move-freely-06

Change the number at the end to match the issue. Save the file when you're done (Cmd+S or Ctrl+S).

Don't change anything inside double curly brackets, such as {{ unsubscribe_link }} or {{ open_tracking_block }}. Shopify fills these in when it sends.
5

Create the email in Shopify

  1. In Shopify admin, go to Marketing → Create campaign → Shopify Email. (In some stores you'll find it under Apps → Shopify Messaging.)
  2. When asked to choose a template, select Code your own.
  3. Click Import and choose the email file you just saved. You can also copy everything in the file (Cmd+A, then Cmd+C) and paste it into the code box.
  4. Check the preview. You should see the logo, the photo and the green and lime design.
No "Code your own" option? Shopify is still rolling it out, so some stores don't have it yet. Contact Shopify Support and ask them to turn on custom-coded emails for Shopify Email.
6

Add the subject line, preview text and audience

  1. Copy the subject line and preview text for this email from the schedule on the last page into Shopify's fields. The preview text is the short line people see next to the subject in their inbox.
  2. Check the sender name reads X-ZONE New Zealand and the reply address is one you both read. The emails say "Reply to this email", so replies need to reach you.
  3. Under To, choose your subscribers, for example Email subscribers.
7

Send yourself a test

  1. Click Send test and enter your own email addresses. You can add up to five.
  2. Open the test on a computer and on a phone, and if you can, in both Gmail and Outlook.
  • The logo, photos, your photo and the range picture all show
  • No square brackets left anywhere
  • Every button goes to the right page
  • The subject line and preview text look right in the inbox
  • The Unsubscribe link at the bottom works

In Outlook on Windows the headings show in Arial instead of Poppins. That's expected, because Outlook blocks web fonts.

8

Schedule it

Click Review, then choose Schedule and set the date from the schedule on the last page. Pick a time when your customers usually read email, such as 7:30 am or 7:30 pm. Use the same time each week so people know when to expect Move Freely.

If something goes wrong

What you seeWhat to do
Pictures are missing or show as broken boxesCheck the folder address in step 3 ends with /files/ and has no file name or ?v= after it. Check the pictures are uploaded in Content → Files with their original names.
Shopify says open_tracking_block isn't validSearch the file for open_tracking_block and change it to open_tracking, keeping the curly brackets. Shopify's help pages use both names.
Shopify says the unsubscribe link is missingCheck the footer still contains {{ unsubscribe_link }}. Start again from the original file if it was deleted by mistake.
Shopify says the code is too largeThe limit is 50 KB, and each email is about 19 KB, so this shouldn't happen. Check you didn't paste the email in twice.
The email looks like plain text in the previewThe file was probably saved as rich text. Start again from the original file and use step 3's TextEdit tip.
Headings look plainer in OutlookExpected. Outlook uses Arial instead of Poppins. Everything else stays the same.
The email is cut off in Gmail with "View entire message"Gmail clips emails over about 100 KB. Ours are about 19 KB, so check nothing was pasted in twice.

Before the very first send

  • Approve all 13 emails on the approval page, including the stand-in hero photos
  • Your business address is ready to put in every footer
  • The reply address on your emails reaches you both
  • Courier last-order dates for Christmas (No. 03) and the old-price end date (Nos. 01 to 03)
  • The offer for the pre-Christmas sale (No. 04) and the survey link (No. 13)
